name: MD5
description: Unsalted MD5 digest. Fast to compute, no salt, widely rainbow-tabled.

name: SHA1
description: Unsalted SHA-1 digest. Deprecated for security use; fast GPU cracking, rainbow-tabled.

name: MySQL323
description: Old MySQL 3.23 password hash. Extremely weak, effectively a 32-bit-ish search space.

name: MySQL4.1/MySQL5
description: SHA1(SHA1(password)) as used by MySQL 4.1+ / MySQL5 PASSWORD().

name: phpass, WordPress (MD5), Joomla (MD5)
description: Portable PHP password hashing framework used by WordPress, phpBB3, and Joomla (MD5 variant). Iterated MD5 with a salt, cost encoded in the first character after the prefix.

name: md5crypt, MD5 (Unix), Cisco-IOS $1$ (MD5)
description: 1000 rounds of salted MD5 (BSD/Linux crypt $1$). Also used by older Cisco IOS 'type 5' passwords.

name: MD4
description: Unsalted MD4 digest. Cryptographically broken; trivially brute-forced or rainbow-tabled.

name: NTLM
description: MD4 of the UTF-16LE password. No salt. Used for local Windows account authentication (SAM) and as a component of NetNTLM challenge/response.

name: Domain Cached Credentials (DCC), MS Cache
description: Windows Domain Cached Credentials (v1), MD4-based, salted with the username. Lets a domain-joined machine authenticate a user without contacting a DC.

name: SHA2-224
description: Unsalted SHA-224 digest. Rarely used for password storage directly.

name: SHA2-256
description: Unsalted SHA-256 digest. No salt/KDF means it is still fast to brute-force despite SHA-256 being cryptographically strong.

name: descrypt, DES (Unix), Traditional DES
description: Traditional Unix crypt(3) DES hash. 2-character salt, effectively limited to 8 significant password characters. Long obsolete.

name: SHA2-512
description: Unsalted SHA-512 digest.

name: sha512crypt $6$, SHA512 (Unix)
description: glibc crypt $6$ SHA-512 based hash with a configurable round count (default 5000). Default password hash on most modern Linux distributions.

name: Domain Cached Credentials 2 (DCC2), MS Cache 2
description: Windows Domain Cached Credentials v2, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 (10,240 rounds) based, salted with the username.

name: Cisco-PIX MD5
description: Cisco PIX truncated/salted-with-username MD5 hash.

name: Cisco-ASA MD5
description: Cisco ASA MD5 password hash, salted by username.

name: WPA-EAPOL-PBKDF2
description: WPA/WPA2 4-way handshake, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 keyed by SSID over 4096 iterations. Requires a captured handshake (.hccapx/.pcap), not a plain text hash string.

name: LM
description: Windows LAN Manager hash. Uppercases and splits passwords into two 7-char halves with a fixed DES key; catastrophically weak by design and deprecated since Windows Vista.

name: Oracle H: Type (Oracle 7+)
description: Oracle 7-10g DES-based password hash (username used as salt).

name: bcrypt $2*$, Blowfish (Unix)
description: Blowfish-based adaptive hash with a tunable cost factor and built-in 16-byte salt. Deliberately slow, GPU-resistant relative to raw hashes.

name: NetNTLMv1 / NetNTLMv1+ESS
description: Challenge/response format captured from SMB/NTLM network authentication (e.g. via Responder). Crackable back to the underlying NTLM/NT hash.

name: NetNTLMv2
description: HMAC-MD5 based challenge/response captured from SMB/NTLM network authentication. Stronger than NetNTLMv1 but still crackable offline.

name: Cisco-IOS type 4 (SHA256)
description: Unsalted single-round SHA-256 of the password, base64-encoded. Cisco's original 'type 4' implementation omitted salting/iteration, a known weakness later fixed by 'type 8/9'.
common_usage: older Cisco IOS 'enable secret' with type 4 (deprecated by Cisco)

name: AIX {smd5}
description: AIX 'smd5' password hash, salted MD5 variant used in AIX /etc/security/passwd.

name: AIX {ssha256}
description: AIX 'ssha256' salted SHA-256 password hash.

name: AIX {ssha512}
description: AIX 'ssha512' salted SHA-512 password hash.

name: AIX {ssha1}
description: AIX 'ssha1' salted SHA-1 password hash.

name: FortiGate (FortiOS)
description: FortiGate/FortiOS firewall password hash, SHA-1 based with the literal 'AK1' marker prefix.

name: sha256crypt $5$, SHA256 (Unix)
description: glibc crypt $5$ SHA-256 based hash with a configurable round count (default 5000).

name: Kerberos 5, etype 23, AS-REQ Pre-Auth
description: Kerberos 5 AS-REQ Pre-Authentication hash, RC4/etype 23. Obtained via network capture or ASREPRoast-style techniques.

name: Drupal7
description: Drupal 7 password hash: iterated salted SHA-512, phpass-style encoding.

name: RACF
description: IBM z/OS RACF (mainframe security manager) password hash, DES-based.

name: scrypt
description: Memory-hard KDF designed to resist GPU/ASIC cracking via large memory requirements (N/r/p cost parameters).

name: Cisco-IOS $8$ (PBKDF2-SHA256)
description: Cisco IOS 'type 8' password: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 20,000 iterations.

name: Cisco-IOS $9$ (scrypt)
description: Cisco IOS 'type 9' password: scrypt-based, memory-hard KDF.

name: MS Office 2007
description: Microsoft Office 2007 document encryption: SHA-1 based, 50,000 iterations of AES key derivation.

name: MS Office 2010
description: Microsoft Office 2010 document encryption: SHA-1 based, 100,000 iterations of AES key derivation.

name: MS Office 2013
description: Microsoft Office 2013+ document encryption: SHA-512 based, 100,000 iterations of AES key derivation.

name: Radmin2
description: Radmin 2.x remote-admin tool password hash.

name: Django (PBKDF2-SHA256)
description: Django's default password hasher: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a configurable iteration count.

name: PDF 1.1 - 1.3 (Acrobat 2 - 4)
description: PDF 1.1-1.3 (Acrobat 2-4) standard security handler, RC4-40.

name: PDF 1.4 - 1.6 (Acrobat 5 - 8)
description: PDF 1.4-1.6 (Acrobat 5-8) standard security handler, RC4-128.

name: SHA2-384
description: Unsalted SHA-384 digest.

name: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
description: PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA256, iterated. Strength depends heavily on the iteration count used.

name: PostgreSQL CRAM (MD5)
description: PostgreSQL MD5 challenge-response authentication hash, salted with the username.

name: Bitcoin/Litecoin wallet.dat
description: Bitcoin/Litecoin Core wallet.dat master-key hash, AES-encrypted key protected by SHA-512-based key stretching.
common_usage: Bitcoin Core / Litecoin Core wallet.dat files

name: 7-Zip
description: 7-Zip archive password hash, SHA-256 with a large configurable iteration count (default 2^19).

name: PBKDF2-HMAC-MD5
description: PBKDF2 with HMAC-MD5.

name: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1
description: PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA1.

name: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512
description: PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA512.

name: Oracle T: Type (Oracle 12+)
description: Oracle Database 12c+ PBKDF2-SHA512 based password verifier.

name: BSDi Crypt, Extended DES
description: Extended DES-based crypt(3) used historically by BSDi Unix. Adds an iteration count over traditional descrypt.

name: RAR3-hp
description: RAR3 'header-protected' (-hp) archive password hash, iterated SHA-1.

name: RAR5
description: RAR5 archive password hash, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 based.

name: Kerberos 5, etype 23, TGS-REP
description: Kerberos 5 TGS-REP hash (RC4/etype 23), the format extracted in a Kerberoasting attack against service accounts.

name: KeePass 1/2 AES
description: KeePass 1.x/2.x database master-key hash (AES or Twofish, PBKDF2/AES-based key stretching, optionally combined with a keyfile).

name: WinZip
description: WinZip AES-encrypted archive, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 based.

name: DPAPI masterkey file v1 + local context
JKS Java Key Store Private Keys (SHA1)
DPAPI masterkey file v2 + Active Directory domain context
JWT (JSON Web Token)
description: JSON Web Token. The 'eyJ' prefix is the base64 encoding of '{"' and appears at the start of essentially every JWT header. Attacking a JWT means recovering the HMAC secret, not a traditional password hash.

name: WPA-PMKID-PBKDF2
description: WPA/WPA2 PMKID hash, derived without needing a full 4-way handshake capture (clientless attack).

name: PKZIP (Compressed)
description: Classic PKZIP (ZipCrypto) archive password hash. ZipCrypto is cryptographically weak.

name: Kerberos 5, etype 23, AS-REP
description: Kerberos 5 AS-REP hash (RC4/etype 23) obtained from accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled (ASREPRoasting).
